This R Markdown document contains all statistical analysis and visualization to date of Dari's agroforestry project. 

One-way ANOVAs were performed to analyze the effects of agroforestry type (pecan vs. pine), cover crop type (for pecan, pine, and the two sites combined), and tillage (no-till vs. minimum tillage) on biological parameters. Two-way ANOVAs were perforemd to analyze the effects and interactions of tillage and agroforestry type, and tillage and cover crop type on biological parameters. For one-way ANOVAs with significant results, post-hoc testing of multiple comparisons between groups was done using Tukey's HSD test.

Biological parameters (response variables) included microbial biomass carbon (MBC), microbial biomass nitrogen (MBN), 24-hour soil microbial respiration, enzyme activities, microbial necromass, total soil carbon (TC), and total soil nitrogen (TN). Statistical significance was calculated with a significance level of 0.05. 

TC & TN data is not yet available but will be analyzed and incorporated when the instrument is available. 

This document is broken into 5 main sections, each representing a parameter to be analysed (shown in the table of contents), followed by visualizations of summary statistics. Each section starts off with a summary of significant and non-significant results. Within each section, there are 6 main subsections, each representing a statistical comparison:

1. pecan vs. pine (with control), 
2. the 10 cover crop types, combined (with control),
3. the 6 cover crop types used for pecan (with control), 
4. the 4 cover crop types used for pine (with control), 
5. no-till vs. minimum tillage, and
6. two-way ANOVAs (agroforestry type * tillage, cover crop type * tillage).

## Microbial Biomass C

**Significance Summary:**

When considering all 3 seasons of data, the following analyses were found to be significant: 

* Agroforestry Tree Type

The following analyses were not significant:

* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine
* Cover Crop Type - Pecan
* Cover Crop Type - Pine
* Tillage Treatment
* No interaction between tree type and tillage
* No interaction between cover crop type and tillage

```{r Import & Cleaning MBIO-3, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# Data import
mbio3rawNF <- read_csv("toc_tn/2024_01_20/raw/2024_01_20_MJS_Agroforestry_Normal.csv")
mbio3rawF <- read_csv("toc_tn/2024_01_25/2024_01_25_MJS_Agroforestry_Normal.csv")

# Data cleaning for NF
mbio3NF <- mbio3rawNF %>%
  setNames(.[10, ]) %>%
  slice(-(1:10)) 

mbio3NF <- mbio3NF %>%
  mutate(`Sample ID` = factor(`Sample ID`, levels = 1:81))

mbio3NFclean <- mbio3NF %>%
  mutate(`Result(TC)` = as.numeric(`Result(TC)`),
         `Result(TN)` = as.numeric(`Result(TN)`),
         `Result(IC)` = as.numeric(`Result(IC)`)) %>%
  group_by(`Sample ID`) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Sample_Name = first(`Sample Name`),
            Unit = first(Unit),
            TC_NF = sum(`Result(TC)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            TN_NF = sum(`Result(TN)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            IC_NF = sum(`Result(IC)`, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(order(`Sample ID`))

mbio3NFclean <- mbio3NFclean %>%
  filter(str_starts(Sample_Name, "NF")) %>%
  filter(grepl("^NF-\\d+-\\d+$", Sample_Name)) %>%
  mutate(ID = as.numeric(gsub("NF-(\\d+)-\\d+", "\\1", Sample_Name)),
         Status = "NF") %>%
  arrange(order(ID))

# Data cleaning for F
mbio3F <- mbio3rawF %>%
  setNames(.[10, ]) %>%
  slice(-(1:10)) 

mbio3F <- mbio3F %>%
  mutate(`Sample ID` = factor(`Sample ID`, levels = 1:81))

mbio3Fclean <- mbio3F %>%
  mutate(`Result(TC)` = as.numeric(`Result(TC)`),
         `Result(TN)` = as.numeric(`Result(TN)`),
         `Result(IC)` = as.numeric(`Result(IC)`)) %>%
  group_by(`Sample ID`) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Sample_Name = first(`Sample Name`),
            Unit = first(Unit),
            TC_F = sum(`Result(TC)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            TN_F = sum(`Result(TN)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            IC_F = sum(`Result(IC)`, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(order(`Sample ID`))

mbio3Fclean <- mbio3Fclean %>%
  filter(str_starts(Sample_Name, "F")) %>%
  filter(grepl("^F-\\d+-\\d+$", Sample_Name)) %>%
  mutate(ID = as.numeric(gsub("F-(\\d+)-\\d+", "\\1", Sample_Name)),
         Status = "F") %>%
  arrange(order(ID))

# Combining NF and F
mbio3 <- merge(mbio3Fclean, mbio3NFclean, by = "Sample ID", suffixes = c("_F", "_NF"))

# Cleaning combined data
mbio3 <- mbio3 %>%
  dplyr::select(-Sample_Name_NF, -Status_F, -Status_NF, -Unit_F, -Unit_NF, -'Sample ID')

mbio3$Sample_Name_F <- sub("^F-", "", mbio3$Sample_Name_F)

mbio3 <- mbio3 %>% rename(ID = ID_F, 'Protocol ID' = 'Sample_Name_F') %>% dplyr::select(-ID_NF)

# mbio3 <- mbio3 %>%
#  rename(TC_F = TC, TN_F = TN, IC_F = IC,
#         ID = ID_F) %>%
#  select(-ID_NF) %>%  select(-'Sample ID') 

mbio3 <- mbio3 %>%
  mutate(ID = factor(ID, levels = 43:64)) %>%
  arrange(ID)

# Combine with sample info... import sample key first
key <- read_csv("sample_key1_Murray.csv")

key <- key %>% rename(ID = "Lab ID")

# combine sample key and data by lab ID
mbio3 <- mbio3 %>% merge(., key, by = "ID")

# factorizing ID and treatments
mbio3$agro_treatment <- as.factor(mbio3$agro_treatment)
mbio3$agro_type <- as.factor(mbio3$agro_type)
mbio3$cc_treatment <- as.factor(mbio3$cc_treatment)
mbio3$cc_type <- as.factor(mbio3$cc_type)
mbio3$tillage <- as.factor(mbio3$tillage)
mbio3$ID <- as.factor(mbio3$ID)

# Now, convert to a dry soil mass basis 

# Vol of K2SO4 solution (35 mL)
vol <- 35

# Import masses
mbio3_mass <- read_xlsx("toc_tn/2024_01_20/AG_2023_CFI_Mass.xlsx")

# Clean mass data
mbio3_mass_clean <- mbio3_mass %>%
  mutate(Mass_NF = ifelse(Status == "Non-Fumigated", `Soil Mass (g)`, NA),
         Mass_F = ifelse(Status == "Fumigated", `Soil Mass (g)`, NA))

# Create new columns for Mass_NF and Mass_F
merged_data3 <- merge(mbio3, mbio3_mass_clean[, c("Protocol ID", "Mass_NF", "Mass_F")], by = "Protocol ID", all.x = TRUE)

library(data.table)
setDT(merged_data3)

merged_data3 <- merged_data3[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA else first(na.omit(x))), by = 'Protocol ID']

# Calculating gravimetric water constant
mbio_theta3 <- read_xlsx("toc_tn/2024_01_20/AG_2023_CFI_ThetaG.xlsx")

mbio_theta3 <- mbio_theta3 %>% rename('ID' = 'Internal ID', 'Wet Mass (g)' = 'Soil Mass (g)', 'Dry Mass (g)' = 'Oct3 Dry Soil Mass (g)')

# Subtracting approx. weigh boat mass
mbio_theta3 <- mbio_theta3 %>% mutate(`Dry Mass (g)` = `Dry Mass (g)` - 2.06)

mbio_theta3$ID <- as.factor(mbio_theta3$ID)

merged_data3_2 <- merge(merged_data3, mbio_theta3[, c('ID', 'Wet Mass (g)', 'Dry Mass (g)')], by = "ID", all.x = TRUE)

merged_data3_3 <- merged_data3_2 %>%
  mutate(theta_g = (`Wet Mass (g)` - `Dry Mass (g)`) / `Dry Mass (g)`)

merged_data3_4 <- merged_data3_3 %>% 
  mutate(Dry_Mass_NF = Mass_NF / (theta_g + 1), 
         Dry_Mass_F = Mass_F / (theta_g + 1))

# Convert values in ppm (mg/L) to a per g soil basis (using extractant volume)
mbio3comp <- merged_data3_4 %>%
  mutate(mg_TC_g_soil_F = TC_F * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_F * 1000),
         mg_TC_g_soil_NF = TC_NF * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_NF * 1000),
         mg_TN_g_soil_F = TN_F * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_F * 1000), 
         mg_TN_g_soil_NF = TN_NF * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_NF * 1000),
         mg_IC_g_soil_F = IC_F * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_F * 1000),
         mg_IC_g_soil_NF = IC_NF * ((vol/1000) / Dry_Mass_NF * 1000))

# Incorporate dilution factor of 2 for TC/TN
mbio3comp <- mbio3comp %>% 
  mutate(mg_TC_g_soil_F = mg_TC_g_soil_F * 2,
         mg_TC_g_soil_NF = mg_TC_g_soil_NF * 2,
         mg_TN_g_soil_F = mg_TN_g_soil_F * 2,
         mg_TN_g_soil_NF = mg_TN_g_soil_NF * 2)

# Add TOC column
mbio3comp <- mbio3comp %>% 
  mutate(mg_TOC_g_soil_F = mg_TC_g_soil_F - mg_IC_g_soil_F,
         mg_TOC_g_soil_NF = mg_TC_g_soil_NF - mg_IC_g_soil_NF)

# Calculate MBIO_C and MBIO_N using extraction efficiency factor of 0.45
mbio3comp <- mbio3comp %>% 
  mutate(MBIO_C = (mg_TOC_g_soil_F - mg_TOC_g_soil_NF)/ 0.45,
         MBIO_N = (mg_TN_g_soil_F- mg_TN_g_soil_NF)/ 0.45)

# Checking if we have non-negative data
nrow(mbio3comp %>% filter(is.na(MBIO_C) == FALSE))
nrow(mbio3comp %>% filter(MBIO_C > 0))
nrow(mbio3comp %>% filter(is.na(MBIO_N) == FALSE))
nrow(mbio3comp %>% filter(MBIO_N > 0))

# Getting averages per sample (across 3 replicates) 
mbio3avg <- mbio3 %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(TC_NF = mean(TC_NF),
            TN_NF = mean(TN_NF),
            IC_NF = mean(IC_NF),
            TC_F = mean(TC_F),
            TN_F = mean(TN_F),
            IC_F = mean(IC_F))

# combine sample key and data by lab ID for avg
mbio3avg <- mbio3avg %>% merge(., key, by = "ID")

# factorizing ID and treatments for avg
mbio3avg$agro_treatment <- as.factor(mbio3avg$agro_treatment)
mbio3avg$agro_type <- as.factor(mbio3avg$agro_type)
mbio3avg$cc_treatment <- as.factor(mbio3avg$cc_treatment)
mbio3avg$cc_type <- as.factor(mbio3avg$cc_type)
mbio3avg$tillage <- as.factor(mbio3avg$tillage)
mbio3avg$ID <- as.factor(mbio3avg$ID)

# Back to regular data... Trimming to non-negative data would be too exclusive... changing to NAs
mbio3 <- mbio3comp %>%
  mutate(MBIO_C = ifelse(MBIO_C < 0, NA, MBIO_C),
         MBIO_N = ifelse(MBIO_N < 0, NA, MBIO_N))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
mbn3 <- mbio3 %>% filter(MBIO_N > 0)
```

```{r Import & Cleaning MBIO-1-2, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# import data... calculations done by Taylor including vol and gravimetric water content in other script and exported
mbio_all <- read_csv("compiled_output_mbio.csv")

# apply extraction efficiency factor of 0.45
mbio_all <- mbio_all %>% 
  mutate(MBIO_C = MBIO_C/ 0.45,
         MBIO_N = MBIO_N/ 0.45)

# rename columns... unit is mg(X)/g soil, not kg soil
mbio_all <- mbio_all %>% 
  rename(ID = lab_id, 
         mg_TOC_g_soil_F = mg_TOC_kg_soil_F,
         mg_TOC_g_soil_NF = mg_TOC_kg_soil_NF,
         mg_TN_g_soil_F = mg_TN_kg_soil_F,
         mg_TN_g_soil_NF = mg_TN_kg_soil_NF)

# subset for non-negative MBC data
# mbc_all <- mbio_all %>% filter(MBIO_C > 0)
# mbn_all <- mbio_all %>% filter(MBIO_N > 0)

# add in season 3 data 
library(data.table)

common_cols <- intersect(names(mbio_all), names(mbio3))
mbio_all_subset <- mbio_all[, common_cols]
mbio3_subset <- mbio3[, common_cols, with = FALSE]

merge_mbio_all <- rbind(mbio_all_subset, mbio3_subset)
  
# Getting averages of season 3 data per bag (across 3 replicates) to match 1 and 2
# Group by 'ID' and calculate the mean for numeric columns
mbio_all_avg <- merge_mbio_all %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(-group_cols()), ~{
    if(is.numeric(.)) {
      # Exclude negative values for columns 'MBIO_C' and 'MBIO_N'
      if(any(names(.) %in% c("MBIO_C", "MBIO_N"))) {
        .[. >= 0] %>%
          mean(na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        mean(., na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    } else {
      .
    }
  }) %>%
  distinct()

# Reset row names
row.names(mbio_all_avg) <- NULL

# Factorizing treatments
str(mbio_all_avg)
mbio_all_avg$ID <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$ID)
mbio_all_avg$agro_treatment <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$agro_treatment)
mbio_all_avg$agro_type <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$agro_type)
mbio_all_avg$cc_treatment <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$cc_treatment)
mbio_all_avg$cc_type <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$cc_type)
mbio_all_avg$tillage <- as.factor(mbio_all_avg$tillage)

# exploratory data analysis: looking at MBIO-C and N across 3 seasons
ggplot(mbio_all_avg, aes(x = ID, y = MBIO_C, color = factor(year))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Sample ID", y = "MBIO_C") +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Year")

ggplot(mbio_all_avg, aes(x = ID, y = MBIO_N, color = factor(year))) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Sample ID", y = "MBIO_N") +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Year")
```

### Agroforestry Type

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# subset to exclude "agroforestry" and "no agroforestry", keeping just the tree types
# aka excluding controls from this comparison
mbc_nocntrl <- mbio_all_avg %>% filter(agro_type %in% c("pine", "pecan"))

# Factorizing treatments
str(mbc_nocntrl)
mbc_nocntrl$ID <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$ID)
mbc_nocntrl$agro_treatment <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$agro_treatment)
mbc_nocntrl$agro_type <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$agro_type)
mbc_nocntrl$cc_treatment <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$cc_treatment)
mbc_nocntrl$cc_type <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$cc_type)
mbc_nocntrl$tillage <- as.factor(mbc_nocntrl$tillage)
```

```{r}
# perform anova 
anova_MBCagrotype <- aov(MBIO_C ~ agro_type,  data = mbc_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBCagrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in microbial biomass C between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine) when considering all 3 seasons of data **(p < 0.001)**.

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# calculate control average for all seasons
mbc_agcntrl_value <- mean(mbio_all_avg$MBIO_C[mbio_all_avg$ID %in% c(42, 44)], na.rm = TRUE)
mbc_agcntrl_value
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Significance letters and Tukey HSD
maxesMBC_Ag <- mbc_nocntrl %>% group_by(agro_type) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(max_value = max(na.omit(MBIO_C)))

hsdMBC_Ag <- HSD.test(aov(MBIO_C ~ agro_type, data = mbc_nocntrl), 
                      trt = "agro_type", group = T)

TukeyHSD(anova_MBCagrotype)

lettersMBC_Ag <- hsdMBC_Ag$groups[order(row.names(hsdMBC_Ag$groups)), ]

# visualize relationship for all seasons
ggplot(mbc_nocntrl, aes(x = agro_type, y = MBIO_C, col = agro_type, fill = agro_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(pch = 16, width = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 19), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18)) +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = expression("Microbial Biomass C (mg C kg"^{-1}*" soil)")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("pecan" = "Pecan", "pine" = "Pine")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#a3d334", "#34aed3"),  
                    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mbc_agcntrl_value, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.35, lineend = "butt", color = "#8c8c8c") +
  annotate("text", y = mbc_agcntrl_value, x = 2.68, label = "No Agroforestry [Control]", hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 5.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(mbc_nocntrl$MBIO_C), 
                           1.3 * max(na.omit(mbc_nocntrl$MBIO_C))),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 4.25)) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesMBC_Ag, aes(x = agro_type, y = 50 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersMBC_Ag$groups), vjust = 0, size = 6.5) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)
```

### Cover Crop Type (Combined)

```{r}
# perform anova for combined for all seasons
anova_MBCCCtype <- aov(MBIO_C ~ cc_type,  data = mbio_all_avg)
summary(anova_MBCCCtype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there was not a statistically significant difference in microbial biomass C between cover crop type when considering both sites combined (pecan and pine) with all 3 seasons of data.

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
  annotate("text", y = mbc_cccntrl_value, x = 10.75, label = "No Cover Crop [Control]", hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 4.25) + 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(mbc_allcc$MBIO_C), 
                           1.3 * max(na.omit(mbc_allcc$MBIO_C))),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 15)) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesMBC_CC, aes(x = cc_type, y = 50 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersMBC_CC$groups), vjust = 0, size = 6) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)
```

### Tillage Treatment

```{r, echo = TRUE, include = FALSE}
# check possible values of variable
unique(mbio_all_avg$tillage)

# subset to remove control
mbcTIL <- mbio_all_avg %>% filter(tillage %in% c("no_till", "min_till"))

unique(mbcTIL$tillage)
```

```{r, echo = TRUE}
# perform anova for all seasons
anova_mbcTIL <- aov(MBIO_C ~ tillage,  data = mbcTIL)
summary(anova_mbcTIL)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there was not a statistically significant difference in microbial biomass C between tillage treatments (minimum tillage vs. no-till) when considering all 3 seasons of data.

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Significance letters and Tukey HSD
maxesMBC_Till <- mbcTIL %>% group_by(tillage) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(max_value = max(na.omit(MBIO_C)))

hsdMBC_Till <- HSD.test(aov(MBIO_C ~ tillage, data = mbcTIL), 
                      trt = "tillage", group = T)

TukeyHSD(anova_mbcTIL)

lettersMBC_Till <- hsdMBC_Till$groups[order(row.names(hsdMBC_Till$groups)), ]

# visualize relationship for all seasons
ggplot(mbcTIL, 
       aes(x = tillage, y = MBIO_C, col = tillage, fill = tillage)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(pch = 16, width = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 17)) +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = expression("Microbial Biomass C (mg C kg"^{-1}*" soil)"),
       title = "") +
   scale_x_discrete(labels = c("min_till" = "Minimum Tillage", "no_till" = "No-Till")) +     scale_fill_manual(values = c("#744700", "#f1c232"),  
                    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesMBC_Till, aes(x = tillage, y = 50 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersMBC_Till$groups), vjust = 0, size = 6.5) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(mbcTIL$MBIO_C), 
                           1.3 * max(na.omit(mbcTIL$MBIO_C))))

# ggsave("thesis_figs/NC_MBC_Till.jpg", width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

### Two-Way ANOVAs

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for MBIO-C using Agroforestry Type & Tillage
anova_MBC_agtl <- aov(MBIO_C ~ agro_type * tillage, data = mbc_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBC_agtl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of agroforestry type and tillage. 

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for MBIO-C using Cover Crop Type & Tillage
anova_MBC_cctl <- aov(MBIO_C ~ cc_type * tillage, data = mbc_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBC_cctl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of cover crop type and tillage. 


## Microbial Biomass N

**Significance Summary:**

When considering all 3 seasons of data, the following analyses were found to be significant: 

* None

The following analyses were not significant:

* Agroforestry Tree Type
* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine
* Cover Crop Type - Pecan
* Cover Crop Type - Pine
* Tillage Treatment
* No interaction between tree type and tillage
* No interaction between cover crop type and tillage

```{r Clean MBIO-N, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# subset for non-negative MBN data
mbn <- mbio_all_avg %>% filter(MBIO_N > 0)
```

### Agroforestry Type

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# check possible values of variable
unique(mbn$agro_type)

# subset to exclude "agroforestry" and "no agroforestry", keeping just the tree types
# aka excluding controls from this comparison
mbn_nocntrl <- mbn %>% filter(agro_type %in% c("pine", "pecan"))

head(mbn_nocntrl)
```

```{r}
# perform anova for all seasons
anova_MBNagrotype <- aov(MBIO_N ~ agro_type,  data = mbn_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBNagrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there was not a statistically significant difference in microbial biomass N between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine) when considering all 3 seasons of data. 

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# calculate control average for all seasons
mbn_agcntrl_value <- mean(mbn$MBIO_N[mbn$ID %in% c(42, 44)], na.rm = TRUE)
mbn_agcntrl_value
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Significance letters and Tukey HSD
maxesMBN_Ag <- mbn_nocntrl %>% group_by(agro_type) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(max_value = max(na.omit(MBIO_N)))

hsdMBN_Ag <- HSD.test(aov(MBIO_N ~ agro_type, data = mbn_nocntrl), 
                      trt = "agro_type", group = T)

TukeyHSD(anova_MBNagrotype)

lettersMBN_Ag <- hsdMBN_Ag$groups[order(row.names(hsdMBN_Ag$groups)), ]

# visualize relationship for all seasons
ggplot(mbn_nocntrl, aes(x = agro_type, y = MBIO_N, col = agro_type, fill = agro_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(pch = 16, width = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 19), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18)) +
  labs(x = "", 
        y = expression("Microbial Biomass N (mg N kg"^{-1}*" soil)")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("pecan" = "Pecan", "pine" = "Pine")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#a3d334", "#34aed3"),  
                    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mbn_agcntrl_value, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.35, lineend = "butt", color = "#8c8c8c") +
  annotate("text", y = mbn_agcntrl_value, x = 2.68, label = "No Agroforestry [Control]", hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 5.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(mbn_nocntrl$MBIO_N), 1.3 * max(na.omit(mbn_nocntrl$MBIO_N))),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 4.25)) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesMBN_Ag, aes(x = agro_type, y = 20 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersMBN_Ag$groups), vjust = 0, size = 6.5) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)
```

### Two-Way ANOVAs

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for MBIO-N using Agroforestry Type & Tillage
anova_MBN_agtl <- aov(MBIO_N ~ agro_type * tillage, data = mbn_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBN_agtl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of agroforestry type and tillage. 

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for MBIO-N using Cover Crop Type & Tillage
anova_MBN_cctl <- aov(MBIO_N ~ cc_type * tillage, data = mbn_nocntrl)
summary(anova_MBN_cctl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of cover crop type and tillage. 

## 24-Hour Microbial Respiration

**Significance Summary:**

When considering all 3 seasons of data, the following analyses were found to be significant: 

* Agroforestry Tree Type 
* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine
* Cover Crop Type - Pecan

The following analyses were not significant:

* Cover Crop Type - Pine
* Tillage Treatment
* No interaction between tree type and tillage
* No interaction between cover crop type and tillage

```{r Import CMIN, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# Data import
cmin_ag <- read_xlsx("Cmin/agro_cmin_calc_new.xlsx")

# Subset to include relevant data
cmin_ag <- cmin_ag %>% dplyr::select(Jar_number, `microg CO2/g dry weight`, `mg CO2/g dry weight`)
cmin_ag <- cmin_ag %>% mutate(ID = as.integer(str_extract(`Jar_number`, "\\d+(?=-)")))

# ID as factor
cmin_ag <- cmin_ag %>% mutate(ID = as.factor(ID))
key <- key %>% mutate(ID = as.factor(ID))

# Combine with key 
cmin_ag_clean <- merge(cmin_ag, key, by = "ID")
cmin_ag_clean <- cmin_ag_clean %>% arrange(ID)

# Making average sheet
cminavg <- cmin_ag_clean %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::summarise("mg CO2/g dry weight" = mean(`mg CO2/g dry weight`, na.rm = TRUE))

# Treatments as factors
str(cmin_ag_clean)
cmin_ag_clean$agro_treatment <- as.factor(cmin_ag_clean$agro_treatment)
cmin_ag_clean$agro_type <- as.factor(cmin_ag_clean$agro_type)
cmin_ag_clean$cc_treatment <- as.factor(cmin_ag_clean$cc_treatment)
cmin_ag_clean$cc_type <- as.factor(cmin_ag_clean$cc_type)
cmin_ag_clean$tillage <- as.factor(cmin_ag_clean$tillage)
```

### Two-Way ANOVAs

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for respiration using Agroforestry Type & Tillage
anova_CMIN_agtl <- aov(`mg CO2/g dry weight` ~ agro_type * tillage, data = cmin_nocntrl)
summary(anova_CMIN_agtl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of agroforestry type and tillage. 

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for respiration using Cover Crop Type & Tillage
anova_CMIN_cctl <- aov(`mg CO2/g dry weight` ~ cc_type * tillage, data = cmin_nocntrl)
summary(anova_CMIN_cctl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of cover crop type and tillage. 

## Enzyme Activities

**Significance Summary:**

The following analyses were found to be significant: 

* Agroforestry Tree Type on BG, PHOS
* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine on BG, PHOS
* Cover Crop Type - Pecan on NAG, PHOS
* Cover Crop Type - Pine on PHOS
* Interaction between tree type and tillage for BG, NAG, PHOS
* Interaction between cover crop type and tillage for BG, NAG, PHOS

The following analyses were not significant:

* Agroforestry Tree Type on NAG
* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine on NAG
* Cover Crop Type - Pecan on BG
* Cover Crop Type - Pine on BG, NAG
* Tillage Treatment on BG, NAG, PHOS

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# Importing data
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = '/Users/murraysternberg/Desktop/R_stuff/thesis/data')
enz_ag <- read_xlsx("/Users/murraysternberg/Desktop/R_stuff/thesis/data/enzymes/AgEnzymes.xlsx", sheet = "ActivityComp")

# Switching rows and columns
activity_ag <- data.frame(t(enz_ag[-1]))
colnames(activity_ag) <- c("BG", "NAG", "PHOS")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# Adding and factorizing ID column
activity_ag$ID <- row.names(activity_ag)
activity_ag$ID_full <- row.names(activity_ag)
activity_ag <- activity_ag %>% mutate(ID = as.integer(str_extract(`ID`, "\\d+(?=-)")))
activity_ag$ID <- as.factor(activity_ag$ID)

# Merge with key
activity_ag <- merge(activity_ag, key, by = "ID")
activity_ag <- activity_ag %>% arrange(ID)

# Factorizing treatments
str(activity_ag)
activity_ag$agro_treatment <- as.factor(activity_ag$agro_treatment)
activity_ag$agro_type <- as.factor(activity_ag$agro_type)
activity_ag$cc_treatment <- as.factor(activity_ag$cc_treatment)
activity_ag$cc_type <- as.factor(activity_ag$cc_type)
activity_ag$tillage <- as.factor(activity_ag$tillage)

# Values as numeric
activity_ag$BG <- as.numeric(activity_ag$BG)
activity_ag$NAG <- as.numeric(activity_ag$NAG)
activity_ag$PHOS <- as.numeric(activity_ag$PHOS)
```

### Agroforestry Type

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# check possible values of variable
unique(activity_ag$agro_type)

# subset to exclude "agroforestry" and "no agroforestry", keeping just the tree types
# aka excluding controls from this comparison
activity_nocntrl <- activity_ag %>% filter(agro_type %in% c("pine", "pecan"))
unique(activity_nocntrl$agro_type)
summary(activity_nocntrl$agro_type)
```

```{r}
# perform anova for BG by agroforestry type
anova_ACT_BG_agrotype <- aov(BG ~ agro_type,  data = activity_nocntrl)
summary(anova_ACT_BG_agrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in activity of the enzyme BG between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine) **(p < 0.001)**. 

```{r}
# perform anova for NAG by agroforestry type
anova_ACT_NAG_agrotype <- aov(NAG ~ agro_type,  data = activity_nocntrl)
summary(anova_ACT_NAG_agrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there was not a statistically significant difference in activity of the enzyme NAG between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine). 

```{r}
# perform anova for PHOS by agroforestry type
anova_ACT_PHOS_agrotype <- aov(PHOS ~ agro_type,  data = activity_nocntrl)
summary(anova_ACT_PHOS_agrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in activity of the enzyme PHOS between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine) **(p < 0.001)**. 

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# calculate control average for BG
act_BG_agcntrl_value <- mean(activity_ag$BG[activity_ag$ID == 44], na.rm = TRUE)
act_BG_agcntrl_value

# calculate control average for NAG
act_NAG_agcntrl_value <- mean(activity_ag$NAG[activity_ag$ID == 44], na.rm = TRUE)
act_NAG_agcntrl_value

# calculate control average for PHOS
act_PHOS_agcntrl_value <- mean(activity_ag$PHOS[activity_ag$ID == 44], na.rm = TRUE)
act_PHOS_agcntrl_value
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE}
# Significance letters and Tukey HSD
maxesBG_Ag <- activity_nocntrl %>% group_by(agro_type) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(max_value = max(na.omit(BG)))

hsdBG_Ag <- HSD.test(aov(BG ~ agro_type, data = activity_nocntrl), 
                      trt = "agro_type", group = T)

TukeyHSD(anova_ACT_BG_agrotype)

lettersBG_Ag <- hsdBG_Ag$groups[order(row.names(hsdBG_Ag$groups)), ]

# visualize relationship for BG
ggplot(activity_nocntrl, aes(x = agro_type, y = BG, col = agro_type, fill = agro_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(pch = 16, width = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18.5), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15)) +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = expression("BG: Potential EEA (nmol activity / g dry soil / hr)")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("pecan" = "Pecan", "pine" = "Pine")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#a3d334", "#34aed3"),  
                    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = act_BG_agcntrl_value, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.35, lineend = "butt", color = "#8c8c8c") +
  annotate("text", y = act_BG_agcntrl_value, x = 2.68, label = "No Agroforestry [Control]", hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 5.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(activity_nocntrl$BG), 
                           1.3 * max(na.omit(activity_nocntrl$BG))),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 4.25)) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesBG_Ag, aes(x = agro_type, y = 150 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersBG_Ag$groups), vjust = 0, size = 6.5) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)
```

### Two-Way ANOVAs


## Necromass

**Significance Summary:** 

The following analyses were found to be significant: 

* Cover Crop Type - Pecan (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)

The following analyses were not significant:

* Agroforestry Type (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)
* Cover Crop Type - Combined Pecan & Pine (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)
* Cover Crop Type - Pine (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)
* Tillage (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)
* No interaction between tree type and tillage (for Total, Fungal, and Bacterial)

```{r Import & Cleaning NEC, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# Data import
setwd("/Users/murraysternberg/Desktop/R_stuff/thesis/data/agroforestry")

necraw3 <- read_excel("2024-01-20_HPLC_AG43-64.xlsx", sheet = "Summary")
necmass <- read_excel("2024-01-20_HPLC_Mass.xlsx")

# Data cleaning
necraw3cleaned <- necraw3 %>%
  dplyr::select("Concentration (uM)", "...3", "...4", "...5", "...6") %>%
  rename(
    ID = "Concentration (uM)",
    GalN = "...3",
    GclN = "...4",
    ManN = "...5",
    MurN = "...6"
  ) %>%
  slice(-1)

necraw3cleaned$ID <- sub("^AG", "", necraw3cleaned$ID)

necraw3cleaned <- necraw3cleaned %>%
  mutate(across(c(GalN, GclN, ManN, MurN), as.numeric))

necmass <- necmass %>% rename(ID = "Internal ID")

# Combining data with mass
necraw3cleaned <- necraw3cleaned %>%
  dplyr::select(ID:MurN) %>%
  merge(., necmass %>% dplyr::select(ID, "Mass post-dry (g)"), by = "ID") %>%
  rename("Mass (g)" = "Mass post-dry (g)")

# Unit conversion
necdata_mg <- necraw3cleaned %>%
  mutate(MurN_mg = MurN * 10^-6 * 251.23 * 1000 * 1/`Mass (g)`,
         ManN_mg = ManN * 10^-6 * 215.63 * 1000 * 1/`Mass (g)`,
         GalN_mg = GalN * 10^-6 * 179.17 * 1000 * 1/`Mass (g)`,
         GclN_mg = GclN * 10^-6 * 179.17 * 1000 * 1/`Mass (g)`)

necdata_mg <- necdata_mg %>%
  dplyr::select(`ID`, MurN_mg, ManN_mg, GalN_mg, GclN_mg)

# Calculating necromass
necdata <- necdata_mg %>%
  mutate(FungalC_mg_g = ((GclN_mg - 2 * MurN_mg) * 9) * 10^-3,
         BacterialC_mg_g = (MurN_mg * 45) * 10^-3, 
         MicrobialResidualC_mg_g = FungalC_mg_g + BacterialC_mg_g)

# Combine with sample info... import sample key first
key <- read_csv("sample_key1_Murray.csv")

key <- key %>% rename(ID = "Lab ID")

# combine sample key and data by lab ID
necdata <- necdata %>% merge(., key, by = "ID")

#factorizing ID and treatments
necdata$agro_treatment <- as.factor(necdata$agro_treatment)
necdata$agro_type <- as.factor(necdata$agro_type)
necdata$cc_treatment <- as.factor(necdata$cc_treatment)
necdata$cc_type <- as.factor(necdata$cc_type)
necdata$tillage <- as.factor(necdata$tillage)
necdata$ID <- as.factor(necdata$ID)

# Saving for Dari's info
# write_xlsx(necdata,"output_sheets\\necromass.xlsx")
```

### Cover Crop Type (Combined)
#### Total Necromass

```{r}
# perform anova for combined
anova_NECCCtype <- aov(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g ~ cc_type,  data = necdata)
summary(anova_NECCCtype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there was not a statistically significant difference in total necromass between cover crop type when considering both sites combined. 

```{r, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE, , include = FALSE}
# calculate control average 
nec_cccntrl <- necdata %>%
  filter(ID == 43) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(nec_cccntrl = mean(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g, na.rm = TRUE))
nec_cccntrl_value <- nec_cccntrl$nec_cccntrl
nec_cccntrl_value

# susbet to remove controls
nec_allcc <- necdata %>% filter(cc_treatment == "covercrop")

# Define colors for tree groups 
pecan_colors <- c("oat" = "#3B6736", "oat-clover" = "#538A4C", "oat-vetch" = "#68AB5F", "rye" = "#7CCA72", "rye-clover" = "#8CDF81", "rye-vetch" = "#9FF893") 
pine_colors <- c("radish" = "#242897", "radish-oat" = "#2C31C6", "radish-rye" = "#3E7DE4", "radish-vetch" = "#6E9FEE")   

tree_colors <- c("oat" = "#3B6736", "oat-clover" = "#538A4C", "oat-vetch" = "#68AB5F", "rye" = "#7CCA72", "rye-clover" = "#8CDF81", "rye-vetch" = "#9FF893", "radish" = "#242897", "radish-oat" = "#2C31C6", "radish-rye" = "#3E7DE4", "radish-vetch" = "#6E9FEE")

# Making CC type into ordered factor for the figure
nec_allcc$cc_type <- as.factor(nec_allcc$cc_type)
nec_allcc$cc_type <- factor(nec_allcc$cc_type, 
                             levels = c("oat", "oat-clover", "oat-vetch",
                                        "rye", "rye-clover", "rye-vetch",
                                        "radish", "radish-oat", "radish-rye", "radish-vetch"))

# Checking reordering
class(nec_allcc$cc_type)
levels(nec_allcc$cc_type)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE}
# Significance letters and Tukey HSD
maxesNECt_CC <- nec_allcc %>% group_by(cc_type) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(max_value = max(na.omit(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g)))

hsdNECt_CC <- HSD.test(aov(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g ~ cc_type, data = nec_allcc), 
                      trt = "cc_type", group = T)

TukeyHSD(anova_NECCCtype)

lettersNECt_CC <- hsdNECt_CC$groups[order(row.names(hsdNECt_CC$groups)), ]

# Plotting the data with modified categories and colors
ggplot(nec_allcc, 
       aes(x = cc_type, 
           y = MicrobialResidualC_mg_g, fill = cc_type, color = cc_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) + 
  geom_jitter(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 2) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15)) +
  labs(x = "", 
        y = expression("Microbial Residual C (mg C g"^{-1}*")")) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("rye" = "Rye", "oat" = "Oat", "rye-vetch" = "Rye-Vetch", "rye-clover" = "Rye-Clover", "oat-vetch" = "Oat-Vetch", "oat-clover" = "Oat-Clover", "radish" = "Radish", "radish-oat" = "Radish-Oat", "radish-rye" = "Radish-Rye", "radish-vetch" = "Radish-Vetch")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tree_colors,
                      aesthetics = c("color", "fill"),
                      breaks = c("Pecan", "Pine")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nec_cccntrl_value, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.35, lineend = "butt", color = "#8c8c8c") +
  annotate("text", y = nec_cccntrl_value, x = 10.5, label = "No Cover Crop [Control]", hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 4.25) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(nec_allcc$MicrobialResidualC_mg_g), 
                           1.3 * max(na.omit(nec_allcc$MicrobialResidualC_mg_g))),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 15)) + 
  geom_text(data = maxesNECt_CC, aes(x = cc_type, y = 0.075 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersNECt_CC$groups), vjust = 0, size = 5) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)

# ggsave("thesis_figs/NC_NEC_Total_CC.jpg", width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warnings = FALSE}
  annotate("text", y = nec_cccntrl_value, x = 7, label = "No Cover Crop [Control]", 
           hjust = 0, vjust = -1, size = 6) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(nec_allcc$MicrobialResidualC_mg_g),
                           max(nec_allcc$MicrobialResidualC_mg_g) + 0.23),
                  xlim = c(0.5, 10)) + 
    geom_text(data = maxesNEC_CCpec, aes(x = cc_type, y = 0.05 + max_value, 
                                    label = lettersNEC_CCpec$groups), vjust = 0) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = 'errorbar', width = 0.1)
```

### Two-Way ANOVAs

#### Total Necromass

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for total necromass using Agroforestry Type & Tillage
anova_NECt_agtl <- aov(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g ~ agro_type * tillage, data = nec_nocntrl)
summary(anova_NECt_agtl)
```

A two-way ANOVA showed that there was not a statistically significant interaction between the effects of agroforestry type and tillage. 

```{r}
# Performing two-way ANOVA for total necromass using Cover Crop Type & Tillage
anova_NECt_cctl <- aov(MicrobialResidualC_mg_g ~ cc_type * tillage, data = nec_nocntrl)
summary(anova_NECt_cctl)
```

A two-way ANOVA was not able to be performed for cover crop type and tillage, likely due to a lack of replication / variability (only one season of data, so only 1 observation for each cover crop / tillage combination).

## Total Carbon

```{r Import TC, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# import data
tc <- read_csv("elemental/tctn_allszn.csv")

tc <- tc %>% rename(ID = lab_id)

# combine sample key and data by lab ID
tc <- tc %>% dplyr::select(ID, perc_c:perc_n) %>%
  merge(., key, by = "ID")

#factorizing ID and treatments
tc$agro_treatment <- as.factor(tc$agro_treatment)
tc$agro_type <- as.factor(tc$agro_type)
tc$cc_treatment <- as.factor(tc$cc_treatment)
tc$cc_type <- as.factor(tc$cc_type)
tc$tillage <- as.factor(tc$tillage)
tc$ID <- as.factor(tc$ID)

# calculating gram per kilogram
tc <- tc %>% mutate(c_gkg = perc_c * 10,
                    n_gkg = perc_n * 10)
```

### Agroforestry Type

```{r, echo = TRUE, results = 'hide'}
# check possible values of variable
unique(tc$agro_type)

# subset to exclude "agroforestry" and "no agroforestry", keeping just the tree types
# aka excluding controls from this comparison
tc_nocntrl <- tc %>% filter(agro_type %in% c("pine", "pecan"))
tc_nocntrl$agro_type <- droplevels(tc_nocntrl$agro_type)
unique(tc_nocntrl$agro_type)
```

```{r}
# perform anova
anova_TCagrotype <- aov(perc_c ~ agro_type,  data = tc_nocntrl)
summary(anova_TCagrotype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in total C between agroforestry tree type (pecan vs. pine) (**p < 0.001**). 

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# calculate control average for all seasons
tc_agcntrl_value <- mean(tc$perc_c[tc$ID %in% c(42, 44)], na.rm = TRUE)
tc_agcntrl_value

tc_agcntrl_value2 <- mean(tc$c_gkg[tc$ID %in% c(42, 44)], na.rm = TRUE)
tc_agcntrl_value2
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# visualize relationship for all seasons
ggplot(tc_nocntrl, aes(x = agro_type, y = perc_c, col = agro_type, fill = agro_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(pch = 16, width = 0.1) + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15)) +
  labs(x = "", 
       y = expression("%C")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("pecan" = "Pecan", "pine" = "Pine")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#a3d334", "#34aed3"),  
                    aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tc_agcntrl_value, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.35, lineend = "butt", color = "#8c8c8c") +
```

### Cover Crop Type (Combined)

```{r}
# perform anova for combined for all seasons
anova_TCCCtype <- aov(perc_c ~ cc_type,  data = tc)
summary(anova_TCCCtype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in total C between cover crop type when considering both sites combined (pecan and pine) **(p < 0.001)**. 

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
# calculate control average for all seasons
tc_cccntrl_value <- mean(tc$perc_c[tc$ID %in% c(41, 43)], na.rm = TRUE)
tc_cccntrl_value

tc_cccntrl_value2 <- mean(tc$c_gkg[tc$ID %in% c(41, 43)], na.rm = TRUE)
tc_cccntrl_value2

# susbet to remove controls
tc_allcc <- tc %>% filter(cc_treatment == "covercrop")

# Making CC type into ordered factor for the figure
tc_allcc$cc_type <- as.factor(tc_allcc$cc_type)
tc_allcc$cc_type <- factor(tc_allcc$cc_type, 
                             levels = c("oat", "oat-clover", "oat-vetch",
                                        "rye", "rye-clover", "rye-vetch",
                                        "radish", "radish-oat", "radish-rye", "radish-vetch"))
# Checking reordering
class(tc_allcc$cc_type)
levels(tc_allcc$cc_type)

# Not removing any here (I would if there were crops with < 3 viable observations)
# mbc_allcc_clean <- mbc_allcc %>% 
#  filter(!(cc_type %in% c("rye", "oat-vetch")))
```

Results of Tukey HSD test and visualization:


```{r}
summary(anova_TNCCtype)
```

The ANOVA revealed that there **was** a statistically significant difference in total N between cover crop type when considering both sites combined (pecan and pine) **(p = 0.01)**.

## Summary Statistics

### Corrplot

This first correlation matrix using corrplot( ) uses data from only the third season (because we only have necromass data for the third season, so otherwise it would have to be removed):

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Making average data frame for enzyme activity
activity_ag$group <- rep(1:ceiling(nrow(activity_ag)/3), each = 3)[1:nrow(activity_ag)]

activity_ag_avg <- activity_ag %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(ID = first(ID),
            BG = mean(BG, na.rm = TRUE),  
            NAG = mean(NAG, na.rm = TRUE),
            PHOS = mean(PHOS, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-group)

# Putting everything together in one
# Merge necdata, mbiocomp, cmin_ag_clean, tc, tn, and key data frames based on the common column "ID"
summary <- merge(necdata[, c("ID", "MicrobialResidualC_mg_g", "BacterialC_mg_g", "FungalC_mg_g")],
                       mbio_all_avg[, c("ID", "MBIO_C", "MBIO_N")],
                       by = "ID", all = TRUE) 

summary <- merge(summary,
                       cminavg[, c("ID", "mg CO2/g dry weight")],
                       by = "ID", all = TRUE)  

summary <- merge(summary,
                       key[, c("ID", "agro_treatment", "agro_type", "cc_treatment", "cc_type", "tillage")],
                       by = "ID", all = TRUE)  

summary <- merge(summary,
                       activity_ag_avg[, c("ID", "BG", "NAG", "PHOS")],
                       by = "ID", all = TRUE)  

summary <- merge(summary,
                       tc[, c("ID", "perc_c", "perc_n")],
                       by = "ID", all = TRUE)  

summary <- summary %>% arrange(ID)

summary$ID <- as.factor(summary$ID)
summary$agro_treatment <- as.factor(summary$agro_treatment)
summary$agro_type <- as.factor(summary$agro_type)
summary$cc_treatment <- as.factor(summary$cc_treatment)
summary$cc_type <- as.factor(summary$cc_type)
summary$tillage <- as.factor(summary$tillage)

# Select only the continuous variables from your summary data frame
continuous_vars <- summary[, c("MicrobialResidualC_mg_g", "BacterialC_mg_g", "FungalC_mg_g", "MBIO_C", "MBIO_N", "mg CO2/g dry weight", "BG", "NAG", "PHOS", "perc_c", "perc_n")]

# To remove rows with missing values:
continuous_vars_no_na <- na.omit(continuous_vars)

# Then calculate the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix <- cor(continuous_vars_no_na)

# Define the category names you want to use
category_names <- c("Total Necromass", "Bacterial Necromass", "Fungal Necromass", "MBC", "MBN", "Respiration", "BG", "NAG", "PHOS", "TC", "TN")

# Set the column names of correlation_matrix to category_names
colnames(correlation_matrix) <- category_names
rownames(correlation_matrix) <- category_names

# Visualize correlation matrix as a heatmap with renamed categories
corrplot(correlation_matrix, type = "lower", tl.srt = 45)
```

This next correlation matrix using corrplot( ) uses data from all seasons (so necromass has been removed): 

